page: Microsoft Azure E128s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The physical architecture comprises 64 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. Memory capacity is 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, and it supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

In benchmark testing, the E128s_v7 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and PassMark CPU score both rank in the top 10% tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 704.78 GB/sec, also placing in the top tier. For database and memory-bound workloads, the server achieves 189.85 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 165.05 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling in the middle 50% average.

This server does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external Premium Storage, which is supported. There are also no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The high density of memory relative to vCPUs provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads by reducing the need to scale up vCPU counts solely to acquire more RAM. The hardware is suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, enterprise applications, and medium-to-large LLM inference tasks, where it achieves 45.31 tokens/sec for 70B model prompt processing.
